scope.why_a_volume_floor: a provider with a handful of claims has a mean intensity that is noise; flagging them generates false positives an investigator cannot act on

signals.top_code_share: z > 2.5 on share of top-two codes

red_team.description: half the ring stops; the rest carry on

dead_rule.verdict: this rule never fires on this book and contributes nothing to the reported precision or recall. It is recorded rather than quietly left in the list, because a three-signal detector where one signal is inert is a two-signal detector, and the threshold (600 min/day) is calibrated for a billing pattern this generator does not produce. Either recalibrate it against real claim volumes or drop it - do not let it pad the rule count.

injected_truth.note: is_fraud and true_em_code are used ONLY to score

finding: Against an adversary who does not know the rules, the detector reaches 95% recall at 91% precision. That number is the least informative one in this report. Once the thresholds are known, the cheapest possible evasion - 'reduced_rate' - takes recall to 18%, a drop of 77%, with no change to the detector at all. A fraud control's honest strength is its strength under adaptation, and reporting the unattacked number alone overstates it by exactly that margin.
